Both marketplaces streamline the loan comparison and application process. Users fill out a single application and are matched with multiple business lenders that meet their criteria, but that is where the similarities end. 

Lendio pairs every applicant with a dedicated funding manager and focuses its entire lender network on business financing. LendingTree draws from a much larger lender network, but only a fraction (roughly 30) are dedicated to business loans specifically, with the rest spread across consumer products. 

This guide compares the features of Lendio and LendingTree that actually affect your experience: what it takes to qualify, how the application itself works, how fast your funding typically arrives, and which financial products Lendio and LendingTree offer.

What is Lendio?

Lendio is an online loan marketplace that matches you with business loan options within its 75+ lender network. The application process starts with a single application, which is sent to applicable loan vendors. You receive offers from different vendors, typically within the same day. By using a single application to apply to many lenders, you can compare multiple loan options without having to tediously apply to every individual lender. 

Business and start-up owners typically use Lendio to expedite the application process, with some loans in as quickly as 24 hours. These loan types include:

  • Business term loans
  • Equipment financing
  • Accounts receivable financing

Lendio’s marketplace is exclusively for business loan vendors, with 11 different business loan types available. Keep in mind, every vendor has different qualifying minimums, and users are not guaranteed the maximum loan amount.

Features that distinguish Lendio from LendingTree

Lendio provides personalized options, assistance, and insight. But beyond those, these three tools really set it apart:

Personal funding managers

Lendio provides a dedicated funding manager who helps you choose a loan option, explains unfamiliar or complex loan terms, offers negotiation advice, and helps with the actual paperwork once you choose a plan.. These funding managers are not chatbots or AI programs, and their role is to be neutral and objective.

Financial management tools

Lendio offers built-in financial management tools like free invoicing, expense tracking, and bookkeeping tools. The app’s self-service model consists of integrated services including bookkeeping software, unlimited invoicing, expense tracking, and profit-and-loss statements, and does not include hidden features or upsells.

Business health analytics

Lendio Intelligent Lending, a proprietary transaction analytics tool, classifies and tabulates a business’s transactions to measure its financial health. This in-depth process involves reading bank statements to detect things like revenue-based deposits and suspicious transactions.

 

Lendio’s business loan focus and large lender network set the platform apart from most other loan marketplaces. Most loan platforms will either have fewer business-specific lenders or will lack personalized assistance integrated into their application process.

What is LendingTree?

LendingTree also uses a single application to match loan seekers with multiple vendors, but it also has a total network of over 300 vendors for consumer loans (about 270) and business loans (about 30), making it the largest online loan marketplace available.

LendingTree’s broad product offerings give business owners the ability to look into personal-type loan options at the same time as business loans, as the process for business-loan applicants is really similar for consumer-loan applicants.

Features that distinguish LendingTree from Lendio

LendingTree’s diverse loan options, financial analysis tools, and extra-detailed lender information give you a wide range of products to choose from and can help with the decision-making process.

Easy comparisons

LendingTree labels its numeric lender comparisons with explicit 'best for' framing, designating specific loans and plans into categories such as the best for fast funding, best for lower-revenue businesses, or best for bad credit. Comparatively, Lendio's public guidance tends to speak to the marketplace as a whole rather than assigning per-lender designation.

Free financial scan

The platform’s LendingTree Spring app provides users with free credit score monitoring, budgeting insights, and personalized financial recommendations. These tools can help you with choosing the optimal loan option, while simultaneously providing an in-depth analysis of both your current business financial and personal financial situations. 

Detailed data per lender

LendingTree provides not only specific application requirements for each individual lender but also their terms and interest rates upfront, not just after the application process. If you prefer to browse different loan types and vendors, you can use this information to find the ideal plans before applying for them.

 

LendingTree offers the widest range of total loan products and categories available on a single platform, creating an easily browseable marketplace where users can compare different types of loans alongside business-specific offerings.

Key differences between Lendio and LendingTree

Lendio and LendingTree offer most of the same business loan products, but they differ in their specializations and overall marketplace sizes.

Lendio is more business focused

Lendio’s specialization is business loans. Lendio’s platform is built for business specifically, and offers around 11 loan products total. 

Their product line covers all of the major business loan options, but you will not find any other loan types on their website. LendingTree also offers about 11 loan products, but their lender network does not only do business loans. 

While LendingTree has the larger overall marketplace, Lendio has a greater number of business loan providers.

New business owners or those needing extra help navigating their business loan options will benefit from Lendio’s dedicated funding managers and assisted application process. Experienced loan borrowers or those also interested in personal loan options will likely find LendingTree’s hands-off, DIY selection process a better fit.

If neither of these platforms appeals to your preferences, consulting with a professional business loan advisor is recommended.

Which is better for your business?

Both Lendio and LendingTree can be viable options for business owners searching for loans, but each platform lends itself better to specific business types, products, and circumstances.

Best for startups: LendingTree

Our top pick for startups looking for business loans is LendingTree. Lendio may have the most lenders, but LendingTree is the friendliest toward startups.

Why Lending Tree is our top pick for startups:

  1. LendingTree’s lower minimum credit score and time-in-business requirements give borrowers the ability to secure startup loans, equipment financing, and other loans. 
  2. Even though Lendio has a higher ceiling for loan amounts, most small businesses and startups will not require the highest end of the funding range.
  3. LendingTree’s startup loan amount starts at $500, which gives small businesses more flexibility for lower-cost needs, compared to Lendio’s $5,000 minimum amount.

Summary and recommendation

Considering all of the information we have covered, below are the overall positives and negatives for each platform:

Lendio pros:
Largest business loan-specific network available
Additional assistance provided through personal funding managers
Greater specialization in business loans for borrowers seeking specific loan characteristics and features
Lendio cons:
Generally higher minimum credit score, income, and time-in business requirements than other platforms
Platform is limited to business loan products only

Ultimately, there is not an objective “better” loan platform, but depending on your unique situation, each platform may have the edge over the other.

Lendio vs. LendingTree FAQs

If your credit score and annual income are already well-established, you are searching for specific loan terms, or you simply require additional support, Lendio is going to be the better fit for small business loans. If you have a lower credit score or annual income, or simply prefer to browse and research loan options independently, LendingTree’s format and style is likely going to be the better option.

No! Both platforms use soft-credit pulls to assess eligibility before the actual application process, with a hard-credit pull not being initiated until you have decided on a plan you would like to formally accept.

Yes, Lendio and LendingTree are both free to use. They are both free services that host a marketplace for loans, but they are not actual loan providers themselves. Instead, they take a small cut of the income that providers make by using their platforms.

Definitions

  • Accounts receivable financing: Funding based on money your customers owe you for unpaid invoices.
  • Business term loans: A lump-sum business loan you repay with interest over a set period.
  • Equipment financing: A loan used to buy business equipment, with the equipment typically serving as collateral.
  • Prime rate: A benchmark interest rate banks use to help set rates on business loans and other financing.
  • Soft credit pull: A credit check that lets a lender review your credit without affecting your credit score.
